To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
higher levels of BMI were related to better cognitive function in HIV-infected and -uninfected women.
in women with HIV infection, lower body mass index (underweight) was associated with poorer performance on Trails A, TrailsB, and Symbol Digit Modality Test.
in middle-aged women with chronic HIV infection, BMI is differentially associated with Trails A, TrailsB, Stroop, and SDMT performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying factors that may influence the cognitive function of women with HIV infection.
the impact of anthropometric measures and HIV on cognitive function.
the effects of HIV infection and HIV treatment on cognition in middle-aged women.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the association between BMI and cognition is complex.
BMI is related to cognitive function among women at midlife with long-standing HIV infection.
BMI is associated with cognition, however the relationship is complex and may be dependent upon the type of cognitive test used and the population being tested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV+ and HIV− women with a BMI < 22 kg/m2 had poorer cognitive performance.

HIV+ women with a BMI < 20 kg/m2 have poorer cognitive function than those with a BMI of 20–24.9 kg/m2 and that HIV+ women who are obese (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m) perform better on cognitive tasks than HIV+ women with BMIs between 25 and 29.9 kg.
the relationship between BMI and cognitive function in middle-age is complex and differs by HIV status.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BMI is associated with cognition among middle-aged HIV+ and HIV− women.
the relationship of BMI and cognition in HIV+ individuals may be different from the general population and that the direction of this association is not necessarily straightforward.
BMI is associated with cognitive function in HIV-infected women, and that this association differs by cognitive domain.
